lore: Kelvaros — the Bruised Realm — is a continent of jagged coasts, ancient mountain belts and a great inland Rift Sea. For eight centuries after the Sundering of the Old Kings, its peoples have fractured and re-forged themselves into a mosaic of empires, marches, tribal khanates and hidden fanes. Five great powers hold sway; a hundred lesser lords chafe against them.

religions.name: Ordinion of the Twelve Flames
religions.description: Cathedral faith of the civilised realms.
religions.lore: Founded by the martyr-prophet Ordis at the Kindling of Solmyr in 1E 214, the Ordinion venerates twelve flames of virtue — Mercy, Iron, Harvest, Song, Vigil, Toil, Bloom, Judgement, Silence, Sail, Hearth and Ash. Its seat is the Basilica of Twelvefold Light in Solmyr. Priests are marked at ordination with a small brand on the palm.

religions.name: Karnathi Sun-Doctrine
religions.lore: The Karnathi hold that Ka-Namar, the Unblinking, is the sole eye of creation and that shadow is heresy given form. Their calendar is measured in Blazes, and their temples are stepped ziggurats of pale sandstone. The Grand Muezzin-of-Fires in Tal-Qadis holds spiritual primacy.

religions.name: Veyral Path
religions.description: Druidic faith of the deep forests.
religions.lore: The Veyral teach that the Wilds and the Kin are two halves of one breath. There is no clergy — only the Green Convocation, an assembly of grove-keepers who meet each Bloom-tide beneath the Mother-Yew of Aelvarim. Practitioners bear a leaf-scar across the throat.

religions.name: Old Stone Faith
religions.description: Oldest religion; mountain and northern pagan.
religions.lore: Older than the Twelve Flames by a thousand winters, the Old Stone Faith worships the frost-carved standing stones said to hold the voices of the first mortals. Its rites are austere: circle-walking at dawn, salt-libations at dusk, and the Long Watch before winter.

religions.name: Cult of the Deep Fathom
religions.description: Seafarers' faith; the Drowned King in the trench.
religions.lore: Sailors, corsairs and coastal reavers swear by the Drowned King, a chained titan said to sleep in a lightless trench beneath the Rift Sea. The devout are tattooed with fathom-marks and, upon death, are weighted with iron and given to the waters.

religions.name: Ashen Covenant
religions.description: Heretical splinter of the Ordinion; embraces suffering.
religions.lore: Condemned as heretical by the Basilica in 3E 411, the Ashen Covenant holds that the Twelve Flames burn wrongly — that only ash remains after all fire, and thus ash is the truest sacrament. Its adherents wear grey and rub cinder into their brows before speech.

religions.name: Dhrenic Ancestrism
religions.description: Tribal ancestor worship of the steppe and northern wildlands.
religions.lore: The steppe-clans, fen-lords and northern barbarians revere the Twelve Grandfathers — mythic founding chieftains whose spirits are said to ride the wind. Each moot begins with the Naming, a recital of ancestry going back at least three generations.

religions.name: Wyrmbound Creed
religions.description: Dragon worship of the Drakenspur peaks.
religions.lore: A cult that once burnt whole villages for tribute to Ozarel, the Rust-Scaled dragon said to slumber beneath the tallest Drakenspur peak. Since the Purging of 3E 702 the creed has retreated to hidden shrines, but its adherents still bind their forearms in copper wire in Ozarel's honour.

nations.name: Empire of Orthengard
nations.motto: From the Iron Spine, Iron Rule
nations.description: The dominant power of eastern Kelvaros — an iron-forged empire seated on the Iron Spine mountains.
nations.lore:
Orthengard rose from the ashes of the Third Sundering when the warlord Kaskan the Unbroken hammered nine feuding houses into a single crown at the Council of Ash-Iron in 1E 486. The empire's spine — literally — is the great Iron Spine Range that shields it from northern raiders; its lifeblood is the sacred river Kelvarne, whose waters are said to have been blessed by the Twelve Flames themselves.

For four centuries the Twelvefold Throne has expanded south and west, swallowing lesser kingdoms into vassalage. Its army — the Legions of Ash-Iron — is drawn from a hereditary caste of iron-branded soldiers who may not marry outside their legion. The current emperor, Aureth IV, is a cautious scholar-king who has spent his reign consolidating the marches and quietly starving the heretical Ashen Covenant of its patrons.

Orthengard's rivalries are old: it has fought seven declared wars with the Sultanate of Qadi-Sharr over the pass-fortresses of the Iron Spine, and it regards the Kingdom of Volmarr with the wary respect one gives an old wolf.

nations.name: Kingdom of Volmarr
nations.motto: What the Cold Made, the Cold Keeps
nations.description: Coastal fjord kingdom of long-hulled ships and Ancestor-Stone worship.
nations.lore:
Volmarr was forged when the sea-jarl Halgar the Elder united the fjord clans in 2E 018 by the simple expedient of sinking every rival ship in the Fjord Reach. His descendants — the House of Halgarim — have ruled for eight hundred years with the aid of a hereditary council of ship-jarls.

The Volmar are the last great practitioners of the Old Stone Faith; their kings are crowned atop the Ancestor-Stone of Grimhal, where each new monarch stands vigil for a full winter night. They are seafarers first, and their long-hulled skorne-ships dominate the northern trade lanes.

Halgar the Silver-Beard, the current king, is now in his eighty-first year and has no acknowledged heir. Three of his ship-jarls quietly circle the throne like gulls; a succession war is expected within the decade.

nations.name: Sultanate of Qadi-Sharr
nations.description: Sun-worshipping sultanate ruling the Great Kelvaran Desert.
nations.lore:
The Sultanate of Qadi-Sharr rose in 2E 341 when the desert-prophet Selim-Ka the First united the twelve nomadic wazir-clans under a single green banner. The sultanate is technically an elective monarchy: upon each sultan's death the wazir-council convenes at the Ziggurat of Tal-Qadis to choose from the eligible male-line descendants. In practice the Selim-Ka line has held the throne unbroken for four centuries.

Qadi-Sharr is wealthy beyond its arid reputation — its caravans control the Cinnamon Road that binds the eastern coast to the western fjords, and its sun-glass artisans are considered the finest on the continent. Its army combines heavy sun-glass cavalry with the feared Muezzin-Guards, warrior-priests who fight blindfold against the shadow.

Selim-Ka IV is famously patient: he has spent his reign quietly strangling Orthengardian trade routes rather than open war. Analysts in Solmyr believe he waits only for Aureth IV to falter before striking north.

nations.name: Confederacy of the Sylvan Reach
nations.description: Loose confederacy of Emberpine forest realms bound by the Veyral Path.
nations.lore:
The Sylvan Reach is less a state than a covenant: in 2E 604 the four great forest-lords of the Emberpine met beneath the Mother-Yew of Aelvarim and swore the Bough-Oath — that they would defend the Deepwood together and otherwise leave one another alone. That oath has held, imperfectly, ever since.

The Reach is ruled in council by the Speaker-in-Green, a lifetime post chosen by acclamation at each Bloom-tide. The current Speaker, Meilith Aelvarim, is only the fourth woman to hold the role and is famed for having single-handedly negotiated the peace of the Charred Cantons in 3E 878.

The Reach's armies are small but the Deepwood is its greatest weapon: no invading force in six hundred years has taken more than the woodland's shallow edge. Its rivalry with the Sultanate of Qadi-Sharr is old and cold — the desert-folk consider the Reach a haven for shadow-heretics.

nations.name: Theocracy of Solmyr
nations.description: Theocratic seat of the Ordinion of the Twelve Flames.
nations.lore:
Solmyr is the mother-realm of the Ordinion of the Twelve Flames, founded in 1E 214 when the martyr-prophet Ordis kindled the First Flame in the ruins of an older city whose name is not spoken. It is ruled by the Ordinat — a lifetime religious sovereign chosen by the Conclave of Twelve.

Solmyr is not the largest realm, but it is spiritually pre-eminent: every monarch in Kelvaros save the Karnathi and the Volmar has been crowned with the blessing of the Basilica. The Templar-March of Kaldros, its sworn militant order, has intervened in twenty-eight recorded wars.

Ordinat Miriach XIV is a former Templar of Kaldros — a warrior turned cleric — and his reign has hardened the Basilica against the Ashen Covenant. Whispers say he plans to declare a Twelfth Kindling, a rite that has been performed only twice in eight hundred years, both times immediately preceding continental war.

nations.name: Duchy of Kern-Vareth
nations.description: Chief vassal-duchy of Orthengard; ancestral seat of the Vareth cadet lineage.
nations.lore: Kern-Vareth was granted to the second son of Kaskan the Unbroken in 2E 118 and has remained the empire's most loyal vassal ever since. Its duke sits at the emperor's left hand at every Council of Ash-Iron. The current duke, Aldrin, is a childhood friend of Emperor Aureth IV and is expected to be named Regent should the ailing emperor die before naming an heir.

nations.name: Margraviate of Ostenmark
nations.description: Frontier march guarding Orthengard's northern approaches.
nations.lore: The Margraviate of Ostenmark was carved from conquered barbarian lands in 2E 245 as a permanent frontier bulwark. Its rulers hold the hereditary right to raise levies without imperial writ — a privilege granted so they may repel raids from the Barbarian Confederacy of Ghurr, whose horsemen still test the border every third summer.

nations.name: Principality of Threnhold
nations.description: Old princely house predating the empire; retained autonomy as vassal.
nations.lore: Threnhold's princes trace their line to before the Third Sundering. When Kaskan the Unbroken forged the empire, the then-Prince Halvarim knelt voluntarily in exchange for perpetual princely dignity and exemption from the iron-branding of the legions. The bargain has held for four centuries and is renewed at each imperial coronation.

nations.name: Free City of Iskal
nations.description: Merchant-Doge city holding autonomous vassalage under Orthengard.
nations.lore: Iskal is a coastal merchant-oligarchy whose charter allows it to rule itself in exchange for a substantial annual tribute and the right to impress its fleet in imperial war. Its Doges are elected for six years by the Council of Guilds; the current Doge, Marek Iskalim, is a fourth-generation banker whose family holds forty percent of imperial debt.

nations.name: Jarldom of Skorne
nations.description: Ship-jarldom holding the harbour of Skorne-Anchor.
nations.lore: Skorne holds the mother-harbour of the Volmar longfleet — every warship of the kingdom is launched from its slipways. Its jarl commands the hereditary Admiralty of the Reach. Ragnhal is one of the three ship-jarls circling Halgar the Silver-Beard's succession.

nations.name: Duchy of Ravnhal
nations.description: Raven-banner duchy of the eastern fjords.
nations.lore: Ravnhal's house-sign is the raven, and it maintains a hereditary rookery at Ravnholt whose birds are trained to carry messages across the whole kingdom. Duchess Ynga is Halgar's own niece and one of three succession claimants.

nations.name: Barony of Weissfjord
nations.description: Ice-locked silver-mining barony of the far western fjords.
nations.lore: Weissfjord's silver mines — carved directly into the fjord walls — supply the Volmar treasury. The barony is ice-locked six months of every year, but its wealth per capita is the highest in the kingdom.

nations.name: Emirate of Ez-Kahar
nations.description: Wealthiest vassal of the Sultanate; hub of the Cinnamon Road.
nations.lore: Ez-Kahar is the chief caravan-city of the Cinnamon Road, and its emirs have historically been the sultanate's richest subjects. The current emir, Rashid, is a cousin of the sultan and a private patron of the sun-glass artisans.

nations.name: Beylik of Tamûr
nations.motto: Where the Palms Meet, We Rest
nations.description: Oasis-beylik of the western desert.
nations.lore: Tamûr is a ring of date-palms around the great oasis of Tamûr-al-Sarr, and its bey holds hereditary rights over the oasis waters — a position of quiet power throughout the sultanate.

nations.name: Waziriate of Selkanth
nations.description: Southern desert waziriate; the sultanate's military academy.
nations.lore: Selkanth trains the Muezzin-Guards — the warrior-priests who fight blindfold against shadow. Wazir Aisha is the first woman ever to hold the post; her appointment in 3E 884 caused a minor schism among the traditionalist muezzin.

nations.name: Wardenship of Hollowreach
nations.description: Northern warden-realm of the Emberpine.
nations.lore: Hollowreach's wardens keep the northern paths of the Emberpine and are sworn to challenge any armed party that enters without leave. Their hereditary bow-guard, the Hollow-Watch, numbers just three hundred but is said to be worth ten times that number in the deepwood.

nations.name: Enclave of Thornhaven
nations.description: Fortified thorn-fen enclave; the Reach's southern shield.
nations.lore: Thornhaven's outer walls are living hedges of ironthorn, said to move against invaders. Its Speaker holds the ceremonial title of Shield of the Deepwood and is by tradition consulted before any war-vote of the Green Convocation.

nations.name: Grove-Kingdom of Aelvarim
nations.description: Ancient grove-kingdom of the Aelvarim line; birthplace of the Veyral Path.
nations.lore: The Aelvarim line has kept the Mother-Yew for a thousand years; they are the only hereditary monarchy within the Sylvan Confederacy and by ancient compact provide the Speaker-in-Green in one out of every four terms.

nations.name: Prelacy of Ostium
nations.description: Southern port-prelacy of Solmyr; second city of the theocracy.
nations.lore: Ostium is the theocracy's window on the Rift Sea and its second-most populous city. Its Prelate is by ancient charter the second voice in the Conclave of Twelve and is traditionally next in line for the Ordinat's throne.

nations.name: Templar-March of Kaldros
nations.description: Militant order-state; the Ordinat's sword-arm.
nations.lore: Kaldros is technically a religious order, not a state; its Grand Templar is a life-appointed office. But by long tradition its lands are treated as a march of Solmyr. The current Grand Templar, Osrik, was raised at the same brotherhood as Ordinat Miriach XIV and is his personal ally.

nations.name: Cantonment of Belkharim
nations.description: Frontier cantonment guarding Solmyr's eastern march against the steppe.
nations.lore: Belkharim was raised as a fortified cantonment in 2E 812 to hold back the raids of the Khanate of Uzarim, and its garrison has never in three centuries been reduced below full strength.

nations.name: Kingdom of Vaenmark
nations.description: Rugged highland kingdom of the Karim range; last of the free stone-kings.
nations.lore: Vaenmark is the last stone-king realm outside Volmarr's orbit — a rugged highland kingdom of terraced barley and long feuds. It has resisted Orthengardian annexation three times, always at ruinous cost. King Radomir has secretly negotiated a defensive pact with the Sultan of Qadi-Sharr — a fact no Orthengardian spymaster yet knows.

nations.name: Grand Duchy of Threnwold
nations.description: Wooded grand duchy between the Iron Spine and the Karim Highlands.
nations.lore: Threnwold's grand dukes have kept their independence by playing the empire and Vaenmark against one another for six centuries. The current Grand Duke, Halvar, is famed for a personal library of six thousand scrolls — the largest secular collection in Kelvaros.

nations.name: Free City of Merevault
nations.description: Coast-city republic of the Deep Fathom cult; famed navy for hire.
nations.lore: Merevault's Doges are elected for life by the Fathom-Council of ship-captains and its navy — small but expert — is available to any bidder. The city venerates the Drowned King openly, a fact that makes visiting Ordinion clerics deeply uncomfortable.

nations.name: Republic of Sarkathil
nations.description: Merchant-republic on the Rift Sea; hires the Grey Wardens as its army.
nations.lore: Sarkathil is ruled by an elected First Consul and a Council of Fifty. It maintains no standing army but retains the mercenary Grey Wardens on permanent contract — an arrangement that has held for one hundred and forty years.

nations.name: Kingdom of Andros-Vel
nations.description: Central small kingdom, wedged between empires; famed swordsmiths.
nations.lore: Andros-Vel's blade-smiths forge the finest swords in Kelvaros; every Ordinion Templar carries an Andros blade at ordination. Queen Ulyria has reigned for thirty-one years by playing all four neighbouring giants against one another with a diplomat's genius bordering on witchcraft.

nations.name: Duchy of Corregar
nations.description: Small border-duchy at the empire's western march.
nations.lore: Corregar is a buffer duchy that has changed hands between Orthengard and Vaenmark eleven times over four centuries. Duke Tallis is the first ruler in living memory to be trusted by both empires simultaneously.

nations.name: Prince-Bishopric of Halgart
nations.description: Small church-state where the bishop is also secular sovereign.
nations.lore: Halgart was elevated to independent prince-bishopric in 2E 559 as a reward for the local bishop's heroic defence against Ashen Covenant heretics. Its ruler is elected for life by the Cathedral Chapter.

nations.name: County of Marreth
nations.description: Tiny independent county; the smallest sovereign realm on the continent.
nations.lore: Marreth is Kelvaros's smallest sovereign realm — a single fortified town and its fields, sworn to no crown since 2E 622 when Count Aldwyn's great-grandfather refused vassalage to Orthengard and paid an enormous sum for perpetual charter.

nations.name: Fenlands Domain of Braeg
nations.description: Marshland lord of the Whispering Fens.
nations.lore: Braeg's fen-lords rule from a floating hall on Osric's Mere and are reputed to keep the last living speaker of the Old Fen Tongue as their seneschal. Outsiders enter the fen at peril: the fen-lords levy no tolls, but the Fen itself is said to.

nations.name: Kingdom of the Windward Isles
nations.description: Island kingdom of the western sea; wave-riders and grey-sailed corsairs.
nations.lore: The Windward Isles are ruled by an elected Sea-King chosen once every seven years by the captains of the Fifty-Longships. The current Sea-King, Halvard, is on his third and final term and is expected to abdicate at the next Council of Sails.

nations.name: Free Kingdom of Ossanic
nations.motto: No Flag, No Master, No Rope
nations.description: Pirate-kingdom of the Sea of Wrecks; sworn to no crown.
nations.lore: Ossanic was founded when the corsair Roric the Elder seized the rocky outcrop of the Fenwyrm Isle and declared himself a king. The kingdom's constitution — such as it is — permits any captain of three or more ships a vote in council. Ordinion, Orthengard and Volmarr have all sent punitive fleets; none have found the corsair-haven.

nations.name: Tribal Federation of Zosk
nations.ruler: Hetman Kurog of the Grey Horse
nations.motto: The Horse Runs, the Grass Bends
nations.description: Confederation of steppe-tribes east of the Rift Sea.
nations.lore: Zosk is a shifting confederation of nine steppe-clans bound by the Grey-Horse Compact of 1E 654. The Grand Hetman is elected every four summers at the Great Moot on the Ashen Steppe. Zoskan light cavalry has sacked Belkharim twice and been repulsed twenty-three times.

nations.name: Khanate of Uzarim
nations.description: Steppe khanate east of Zosk; larger and more centralised.
nations.lore: Uzarim is the larger of the two great steppe realms and has been the sword hanging over eastern Solmyr for a century. Great Khan Berkut acceded in 3E 887 and immediately doubled the standing horse-guard.

nations.name: Emirate of Halaqim
nations.description: Small independent Karnathi emirate; heretical to Qadi-Sharr's doctrine.
nations.lore: Halaqim broke from the sultanate in 2E 704 over a dispute of the Muezzin succession. The emirate maintains its own line of Grand Muezzins and is considered spiritually schismatic. Qadi-Sharr has never reconquered it for fear of igniting a wider sun-doctrinal war.

nations.name: Free City of Emberport
nations.description: Autonomous port city on the Emberline Coast.
nations.lore: Emberport is the busiest port on the southeastern coast and taxes every cargo that passes its lighthouses. Its Doge is elected annually by the Guild of Piers — an office notorious for its short life expectancy.

nations.name: Ordermarch of the Grey Wardens
nations.description: Mercenary state; the finest hired swords in Kelvaros.
nations.lore: Founded by the ex-Templar Kaerin the Elder in 3E 217, the Grey Wardens are Kelvaros's most respected mercenary company. They have a permanent contract with the Republic of Sarkathil and secretly follow the Ashen Covenant — a fact known only to their inner Warden-Circle.

nations.name: Vampiric Duchy of Nakresh
nations.description: Dark duchy of the northern woods; ruled by an ageless bloodline.
nations.lore: Nakresh's ducal line has ruled without succession for eight hundred and twenty years — a fact the neighbouring realms studiously do not discuss. The current Duke, Malviel, was already Duke when the empire was founded. Nakreshi peasants pay a token blood-tithe every mid-winter; in exchange, no outside army has crossed their border in living memory.

nations.name: Necrotheocracy of Vhalarim
nations.description: Ashen Covenant homeland; ruled by grave-regents on behalf of the dead.
nations.lore: Vhalarim was founded in 3E 411 immediately after the Ordinion's excommunication of the Ashen Covenant. Its Grave-Regents rule 'on behalf of the honoured dead', who are consulted through elaborate cinder-rituals. Its neighbours consider it either an abomination or a convenient buffer, depending on the season.

nations.name: Deep-Hold of Grumnar Kal
nations.ruler: Deepwarden Balgrim of the Iron Beard
nations.description: Mountain-hold carved into the Iron Spine; folk of long beards and longer memory.
nations.lore: Grumnar Kal is the oldest continuous polity in Kelvaros — founded in 1E 022, before even the martyr-prophet Ordis. Its people carve their cities into the mountain roots and elect a Deepwarden for life. The hold has never been conquered; even Kaskan the Unbroken went around it.

nations.name: Wyrm-Cult of Ozarel
nations.description: Hidden dragon-cult in the Drakenspur peaks; publicly outlawed.
nations.lore: Officially the Wyrm-Cult was extinguished by the Purging of 3E 702. In truth, its Rust-Priests fled to hidden shrines in the Drakenspur peaks where they still tend Ozarel's copper-wire altars. The cult claims to hold three of the dragon's shed scales as relics.

nations.name: Confederation of the Emberline
nations.description: Loose confederation of six coastal towns along the Emberline.
nations.lore: The Emberline Confederation binds six small port-towns under a rotating First Speaker. It is best known for keeping open trade routes to the island of Cerelith and for producing the amber-lantern glass beloved of the Ordinion clergy.

nations.name: Merchant-Republic of Cerelith
nations.description: Island merchant-republic in the Sea of Snakes.
nations.lore: Cerelith's island holds one of the richest merchant cities on the continent. Its ruling Council of Twelve is drawn from the twelve great trading houses, and the Council seat rotates monthly among them. The republic maintains no army — only an oversized navy.

nations.name: Free Republic of Traxion
nations.description: Small landlocked republic; rare experiment in universal male suffrage.
nations.lore: Traxion is Kelvaros's political oddity: since 3E 214 every freeman over twenty may vote in its bi-annual moot. The neighbouring monarchies regard the arrangement as either dangerous heresy or comic novelty.

nations.name: Barbarian Confederacy of Ghurr
nations.description: Northern barbarian confederacy of raiders and horse-clans.
nations.lore: The Ghurric confederacy has raided the Margraviate of Ostenmark every third summer for four hundred years. War-Chieftain Ghurr Ironmouth is the fourteenth chieftain to bear the name and the first in three generations to have subdued all nine clan-heads under a single banner.

nations.name: Isle-Kingdom of Vaesca
nations.motto: The Isle Answers Only to the Isle
nations.description: Green isle-kingdom in the Sea of Snakes; last matriarchal realm.
nations.lore: Vaesca has been ruled by an unbroken line of queens since 2E 122. Its constitution forbids a king from sitting the throne — a rule that has led to at least one recorded case of a queen-in-name-only crowning a girl-child of two.

nations.name: Free City of Karth-Ulgra
nations.description: Border free city between Orthengard's western march and Vaenmark.
nations.lore: Karth-Ulgra sits at the crossroads of three great empires and has profited enormously by playing them against one another. Its burgomasters are elected for six years and are famed for their beards, which by long tradition must not be trimmed while in office.

nations.name: Duchy of Elmhold
nations.description: Forest-edge duchy on the northern fringe of the Emberpine.
nations.lore: Elmhold is often called the Reach's shy cousin — it follows the Veyral Path but has never joined the Sylvan Confederacy, preferring quiet sovereignty. Duke Rhys is famous for his skill with the elm-longbow.

nations.name: Principality of Thelmar
nations.description: Coastal principality with the finest fleet outside the majors.
nations.lore: Thelmar's princes have quietly built the fifth-strongest fleet in Kelvaros without attracting undue attention. Prince Osric is a maritime scholar who has personally circumnavigated the continent — a feat done only twice before.

nations.name: Kingdom of Corvath
nations.description: Small forest-edge kingdom along the Verdant Marches.
nations.lore: Corvath's kings claim descent from the mythic Green Convocation itself and are crowned in a moonlit grove rather than a hall. Ealdric is the first Corvathi king in a century to have visited the Reach's Bloom-tide.

nations.name: County of Bracken-Hollow
nations.motto: A Small Word, a Long Reach
nations.description: Tiny hollow-county nestled between marshes and forest.
nations.lore: Bracken-Hollow's countesses have ruled without heir-troubles by the curious practice of adopting their successor at the age of twelve, regardless of birth. Milena was so adopted; her successor already stands at her side.

nations.name: Sultanate of Wexil
nations.description: Independent sultanate south of Qadi-Sharr; second Karnathi power.
nations.lore: Wexil broke from the sultanate in 2E 728 under Wexil-ka the Founder and has held its independence by the simple expedient of never fighting a war it could not win. Wexil-ka II is the seventh of his line; the sultans of Wexil name their heirs after themselves by tradition.

nations.name: Theocratic Marches of Ordinion
nations.description: Frontier religious march; a Solmyri splinter that guards the north.
nations.lore: The Theocratic Marches were established in 3E 402 to guard the Ordinion faith along the northern border. Though nominally an autonomous ally of Solmyr, its March-Ordinat sits on the Conclave of Twelve — an oddity that has never quite been resolved by canon law.

nations.name: Demarchy of Hond
nations.motto: By Lot, By Voice, By Law
nations.description: Democracy-by-lot; a strange experiment in southern Kelvaros.
nations.lore: Hond selects its First-Elected annually by lot from among its freeholders — a system considered eccentric but stable. The current First-Elected is a former baker named Wren Halfin who by all accounts is doing a surprisingly good job.

nations.name: Theocracy of Loxmor
nations.description: Small orthodox theocracy sworn to the Ordinion but not to Solmyr.
nations.lore: Loxmor's hierarchs accept Solmyr's doctrine but not Solmyr's political primacy — an old schism that has never quite ripened into full break. Hierarch Volusia has ruled for thirty-two years and has quietly refused to attend the last four Conclaves of Twelve.

nations.name: United Clans of Talabas
nations.description: Southeastern clan union of twelve tribes bound by common law.
nations.lore: Talabas is a rare tribal state that has adopted a written common law — the Talabin Compact of 2E 887. Its Speaker of Twelve rotates every two years among the twelve clan-heads; the current Speaker is a warrior-poet whose battle-verses have become popular even in Solmyr.

nations.name: Tribal Kingdom of Mokhur-Tan
nations.description: Northern tribal kingdom of the far mountains.
nations.lore: Mokhur-Tan is a hereditary tribal monarchy whose king-chiefs are chosen from the eldest son of the eldest son. Mokhur the Younger is the eighth of his line and famed for having personally slain a snow-bear at fifteen.

nations.name: Broken Kingdom of Pridon
nations.description: Kingdom without a king; ruled by a fractious regent council.
nations.lore: Pridon's last king died without heir in 3E 812 and its Regent Council has ruled — barely — for eighty years while three claimants press their rights in slow legal war. Every attempt to crown one has been vetoed by the other two. The population is by now philosophical.

nations.name: Technocratic Republic of Dissenya
nations.description: Republic ruled by its guild of clockwork-artificers.
nations.lore: Dissenya's Artificer-Council rules by the ancient guild-charter. Its clockwork mechanisms are the finest on the continent — every court clock in Kelvaros bears a Dissenyan artificer's mark. The First Artificer, Belloth, is also the finest bronzeworker of his generation.

nations.name: Plombulate of Villivox
nations.description: Small island lead-mining state; a peculiar constitutional oddity.
nations.lore: Villivox is the only 'Plombulate' in Kelvaros — a form of government invented in 3E 344 by the lead-baron Rossic the Elder, in which the ruler is chosen by weighing the candidates in lead ingots on a great public scale. The heaviest candidate wins. It is unclear whether this is a joke or not, but it has held for five hundred and forty years.

nations.name: Confederation of Jib-Jib
nations.description: A confederation of six small forest towns known for their disagreeable politics.
nations.lore: Jib-Jib is named for the doubled-voice of its confederate speakers — six speakers who must all agree for any policy to pass. In practice they rarely do, and Jib-Jib is famously the slowest-moving state in Kelvaros. This is, according to its citizens, a feature.

nations.name: Empire of Drakenmarch
nations.description: Long peninsula 'empire'; strongly linked to the Wyrmbound Creed.
nations.lore: Drakenmarch styles itself an empire though it holds barely more land than a large kingdom. Its Drake-Emperors have historically been the chief secular patrons of the Wyrmbound Creed, and the current ruler, Ozel-Ka the Elder, is rumoured to be the Rust-Priest of Ozarel's own half-brother — a claim officially denied on both sides.

Old wolves eyeing each other; both remember the Sack of Ravnholt in 2E 611.
Ongoing spiritual war; Solmyr excommunicated Vhalarim in 3E 411.
Solmyr suspects (correctly) that Nakresh shelters Ashen Covenant clerics.
Perpetual frontier war; Ostenmark raided every third summer.
Belkharim's garrison has held for a century against Uzari raids.
Schism of the Muezzin-succession; centuries of quiet feud.
Desert-folk consider the Reach a shadow-haven; Reach considers desert-folk fanatics.
Solmyr's Purging of 3E 702 has never been forgiven; the Rust-Priests wait.
Drakenmarch shelters wyrm-cultists; Solmyr calls for their extradition.
Concord of the Twelvefold Throne: Solmyr crowns Orthengardian emperors.
The Templar-March is Solmyr's sword; sacred alliance since 1E 302.
Old Stone Faith pact of the Hearth-Fires; mutual defence since 2E 400.
Secret defensive pact against Orthengard; known to almost no one.
Permanent mercenary contract; renewed every eight years since 3E 217.
Green-Leaf Pact: informal but respected veyral alliance.
Elmhold observes the Bough-Oath informally.
Publicly denied; privately, family ties bind the Rust-Priest and Drake-Emperor.
The Amber-Silk Concord: exclusive trade of amber for silks.
Cinnamon Road Compact: shared tariff schedule.
Fleet-share pact; Thelmari shipwrights build imperial hulls.
Corsair-brother pact; safe waters between the isles.
Ducal cadet branch of the imperial house.
Duchess Ynga is King Halgar's niece.
